\section[anusvar]{\bn{ং} (anusvar) — the ng in \bn{বাংলা}}

\label{lesson:BN-W41-anusvar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \bn{থ} and \bn{ঞ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\bn{বাংলা}} (\emph{bānglā}), \textquotedblleft{}Bengali\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \bn{ং}}
\textbf{\bn{ং}} — \emph{anusvar}, the sound \emph{ng}.

It is inside \textbf{\bn{বাংলা}} (\emph{bānglā}), the name of the language itself. The small mark right after \textbf{\bn{বা}} closes that syllable with \emph{ng}.

\subsection*{Writing: \bn{ং}}
Put your pen on \bn{ং} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\bn{বাংলা}} and point at \bn{ং} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \bn{ং} three times, saying \emph{ng} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \bn{ঞ}, then \bn{ং}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\bn{বাংলা}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \bn{ং}? (\textbf{anusvar}, \emph{ng}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\bn{বাংলা}}, \emph{bānglā}, \textquotedblleft{}Bengali\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bisarga]{\bn{ঃ} (bisarga) — the two dots in \bn{দুঃখিত}}

\label{lesson:BN-W41-bisarga}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \bn{ঞ} and \bn{ং} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\bn{দুঃখিত}} (\emph{dukkhito}), \textquotedblleft{}sorry\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \bn{ঃ}}
\textbf{\bn{ঃ}} — \emph{bisarga}, two small circles one above the other.

It is inside \textbf{\bn{দুঃখিত}} (\emph{dukkhito}), \textquotedblleft{}sorry\textquotedblright{}. Bengali does not say the \emph{bisarga} as a sound of its own here: it doubles the consonant after it, so \textbf{\bn{দুঃখিত}} is said \emph{dukkhito}.

\subsection*{Writing: \bn{ঃ}}
Put your pen on \bn{ঃ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\bn{দুঃখিত}} and point at \bn{ঃ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \bn{ঃ} three times, saying \emph{kk} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \bn{ং}, then \bn{ঃ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\bn{দুঃখিত}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \bn{ঃ}? (\textbf{bisarga}, \emph{kk}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\bn{দুঃখিত}}, \emph{dukkhito}, \textquotedblleft{}sorry\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[jha]{\bn{ঝ} (jha) — the letter inside \bn{বোঝা}}

\label{lesson:BN-W41-jha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \bn{ং} and \bn{ঃ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\bn{বোঝা}} (\emph{bojhā}), \textquotedblleft{}to understand\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \bn{ঝ}}
\textbf{\bn{ঝ}} — \emph{jha}, a \emph{j} with a puff of breath.

It is inside \textbf{\bn{বোঝা}} (\emph{bojhā}), \textquotedblleft{}to understand\textquotedblright{}. Say \emph{boja}, then \emph{bojhā}: the second has the breath.

\subsection*{Writing: \bn{ঝ}}
Put your pen on \bn{ঝ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\bn{বোঝা}} and point at \bn{ঝ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \bn{ঝ} three times, saying \emph{jh} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \bn{ঃ}, then \bn{ঝ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\bn{বোঝা}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \bn{ঝ}? (\textbf{jha}, \emph{jh}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\bn{বোঝা}}, \emph{bojhā}, \textquotedblleft{}to understand\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pha]{\bn{ফ} (pha) — the letter that ends \bn{মাফ}}

\label{lesson:BN-W41-pha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \bn{ঃ} and \bn{ঝ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\bn{মাফ}} (\emph{maf}), \textquotedblleft{}pardon\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \bn{ফ}}
\textbf{\bn{ফ}} — \emph{pha}, a \emph{p} with a puff of breath, and the letter Bengali uses for \emph{f} in borrowed words.

It ends \textbf{\bn{মাফ}} (\emph{maf}), \textquotedblleft{}pardon\textquotedblright{}, in \textbf{\bn{মাফ} \bn{করবেন}}, \textquotedblleft{}excuse me\textquotedblright{}. The word came from Persian, and there \textbf{\bn{ফ}} is read as \emph{f}.

\subsection*{Writing: \bn{ফ}}
Put your pen on \bn{ফ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\bn{মাফ}} and point at \bn{ফ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \bn{ফ} three times, saying \emph{ph} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \bn{ঝ}, then \bn{ফ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\bn{মাফ}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \bn{ফ}? (\textbf{pha}, \emph{ph}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\bn{মাফ}}, \emph{maf}, \textquotedblleft{}pardon\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
